verified.exploit_entry_point: The daemon's authorization middleware (pkg/authorization Middleware.WrapHandler -> Ctx.AuthZRequest / AuthZResponse) in front of the real API router handlers. Hidden cases mount real routes from api/server/router/{swarm,plugin,checkpoint,container}, a representative authentication route, and a response-writing route, register them the way api/server/server.go does, and drive them over HTTP with an in-process authorization plugin that records exactly what it is handed.
sites: pkg/authorization/authz.go:71-79 (declared-length body at or above maxBodySize skips capture)
pkg/authorization/authz.go:144-161 (drainBody returns a nil body with only a warning for an oversized stream)
pkg/authorization/authz.go:172-193 (sendBody keys body visibility on the client-supplied media type)
api/server/router/swarm/cluster_routes.go:22,44,74,128,194,220,316,398,439,475,517 (JSON decoded from the body without a media-type check)
pkg/authorization/response.go:50,120-130,169-204 (buffer flushed to the client before AuthZResponse)
pkg/authorization/authz.go:163-170 (isAuthEndpoint regexp never matches the leading-slash path url.Parse returns)
routes: T1/T2: POST /swarm/init with a body over the limit, declared length and streamed length
T3: POST /swarm/init, /services/create, /plugins/pull, /containers/{name}/checkpoints with a JSON body whose declared media type is not JSON
T4: a response route writing two chunks over the 64KB buffer while the plugin denies
T6: POST /auth (versioned and unversioned) with a credential body
verified.project_tests_run: go test ./pkg/authorization -count=1 (pinned, oracle, alternative, hardening and every check patch)

traps.shape: a request whose declared length is at or above the inspection limit skips body capture entirely, so the plugin decides on an empty body while the handler parses and acts on the full one; coupled must-keep: bodies up to the limit are still shown and delivered, and an over-limit request does not crash the daemon
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the size cap is documented and the in-tree TestDrainBody asserts that an oversized body yields a zero-length capture, so the skip reads as intended behaviour; the plugin still receives the declared length header and could refuse the request itself
traps.realistic_because: the published advisory route; confirmed on the pinned tree through the real middleware and route

traps.shape: the same operation reached with a streamed/undeclared-length body over the limit gets past the call-site guard into the helper, whose full-buffer branch returns a nil body with only a warning; coupled must-keep: legitimate large non-JSON uploads stream through untouched
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the earlier 0-length fix routes chunked requests into the drain helper, so the streamed framing looks covered; the full-buffer branch reads like a normal 'too large to copy' outcome rather than a bypass
traps.realistic_because: the advisory route's streamed form; confirmed on the pinned tree

traps.shape: the client-declared media type decides whether the body is shown to the plugin, but several API handlers decode JSON from the body without enforcing that media type, so a request the daemon acts on is decided by a plugin that saw nothing; coupled must-keep: legitimate JSON routes and large non-JSON uploads keep working
traps.reason_to_dismiss: sendBody documents that bodies are sent only for JSON media types, and most JSON endpoints enforce the type themselves at the top of the handler, so a request with a non-JSON type looks like a client error the plugin need not reason about
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: these handlers have no media-type check at the pinned commit and still have none at upstream HEAD (checked 2026-10-26)

traps.shape: the response adapter flushes buffered output to the client whenever the next write would exceed 64KB, before the plugin's response decision is consulted; coupled must-keep: explicit incremental flushing by a streaming handler still delivers chunks as they are produced
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the 64KB buffer is an explicit memory bound carrying a TODO, and the plugin still receives the status code and headers; every streaming endpoint has to flush as it goes, so 'the plugin only sees the tail of a large response' looks like an accepted limitation
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; upstream HEAD still flushes the buffer before AuthZResponse (checked 2026-10-26)

traps.shape: the authentication-endpoint exclusion that is meant to withhold the credential body is given a path form it never matches, so registry credential material is always shown to plugins; coupled must-keep: the authentication request still reaches the daemon, and credential headers stay hidden
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the plugin is a trusted policy component and the authentication body only feeds registry login, never an authorization decision, so the dead exclusion has no obvious security impact
traps.realistic_because: published fix far site: the earlier fix's own path validation left dead code; later fixed upstream by the published B commit

wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: the protection is about what a plugin is shown, not about which resource a request touches; there is no per-resource identity to confuse
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: the tested surface is request-body and response-body visibility, not read versus write verbs
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: there is no external authority or secret lookup; the plugin is present on every tested request
